mp.pillar: Sustained Dominance: higher positions, longer presence and higher peak positions on Most Popular.
observations: Most Popular barely moved today: no new entries, only PORTALS fell off, and the biggest risers gained a single place.
Steal An Egg (82 days) still leads, ahead of evergreens such as Brookhaven, Murder Mystery 2, 99 Nights in the Forest and RIVALS.
Multi-year games hold the best median pillar percentile (62), while 4-to-12-month games sit lower (35), which keeps the mid-life trough idea alive at low confidence.
The day's small risers are duel shooters (KNIFE DUELS, Murder Duels) and survival or social staples (100 Days At Sea, Welcome to Bloxburg).
patterns: Games pricing most passes above about 90 to 149 R$ and dev products above 79 R$ tend to stay on Most Popular longer; age is a confounder, since older games also price higher.
More complex, more original games tend to hold more days on the chart, and combat PvP and roleplay loops have the best median standing among profiled loops.
A high favorite rate per visit goes with lower positions, because the biggest evergreens turn fewer of their huge visit counts into favorites.
Video observations of long-running hits show two durable styles: near-empty HUD social worlds (Brookhaven, Adopt Me!) and dense progression HUDs (Blox Fruits); it is speculative which matters more.

outliers.note: Tops Most Popular at under three months old with a template loop, the opposite of the age and originality patterns; it is the original of its wave and still updates daily.

outliers.name: Scooter Empire [UPD]
outliers.note: The weakest game on the pillar at 12 days old, likely a young breakout that reached the chart briefly before its reach settled.

te.pillar: Monetization Efficiency: earning a high position with modest CCU (Monetization Score ranks position × CCU, lower is better).
observations: Donation hubs (Summer Donations, Donation Central, Simple DONATIONS) again lead monetization efficiency, with The Company and Elemental Dungeons close behind.
Young survival and horror games (Violence District, Bunker vs Verity, Sarab, Sell Fries!) are the least efficient, earning little for their player counts.
15-to-42-day games have the lowest median efficiency (25) while games past 85 days sit near 58, consistent with revenue catching up with age.
Only one new entry (Jump Showdown) arrived, and the biggest risers moved a single place.
patterns: Dev products priced above 79 R$, servers of 25+ players, redeem codes, detailed descriptions and bracket tags in the title consistently go with higher efficiency, though many of these also mark older, actively run games.
RPGs and combat PvP loops consistently earn more for their CCU, while pet/egg, steal-a-X, '+1' and survival games consistently earn less.
More complex, studio-scale builds consistently monetize better, matching the polished long-running hits in the video observations (War Tycoon, BedWars, Dress To Impress).

Long-running hits in the videos show the shop or currency on the HUD at all times (War Tycoon, Blox Fruits, ABA), suggesting constant purchase visibility is part of durable monetization; this remains speculative.

outliers.name: Morioh High
outliers.note: Among the most efficient games at 13 days old, against the age pattern; a small CCU flatters efficiency, and the single 3 PM snapshot may favor it.

outliers.name: [CURE] Violence District
outliers.note: Nearly two years old yet the least efficient game, breaking the age pattern; survival games with few products earn little per player.

tt.pillar: Early Momentum: rapid upward movement on Top Trending, among games 0–4 months old only.
tt.metric: daily position gain on Top Trending
observations: Wash the Car (+38), IT WANTS IN (+25) and Surf And Rescue (+22) led the day's momentum, a mix of idle tycoon, horror and rescue-sim loops.
Nine games entered and ten left, including Adopt Me!, Dandy's World and Tower Defense Simulator, so the chart turned over heavily.
The youngest games (0-14 days) have the best median momentum (84), well above 43-84-day games (42).
Dogs of War fell 55 places after a brief resurgence, the day's sharpest drop.
patterns: Young games built around building or crafting may climb faster, while creature-themed games may climb slower, both new ideas to test with the age effect held fixed.
Co-op young games may hold higher positions among games of similar age (within-age effect +0.62 on a small sample).
'Steal' and 'Egg' titles go with weaker momentum today, in line with the fading steal/egg wave, while '+1' titles do a little better.
Age explains much of the momentum gap: games past six weeks rarely lead, though Wash the Car (60 days) and Surf And Rescue (51 days) are counter-examples.

outliers.name: Wash the Car 🧽
outliers.note: The day's top climber at 60 days old, with no game passes, against the age and pass-count patterns; a simple satisfying cleaning loop may be drawing a late wave.

outliers.name: 100 Player Lava Escape 🔥
outliers.note: Climbed 21 places at almost a year old, outside the young-game pattern; big-server party obbies resurface in waves.

uc.pillar: Breakout Popularity: higher positions within Up-and-Coming.
observations: Chop A Forest, Sell Fries!, Paint a Pancake, +1 Karate Evolution and WRONG WAY! lead, all between 14 and 24 days old.
DIVINE HATCHERS (+45) and HUNTRESS (+44) made the biggest jumps, the latter at 108 days old.
Seven games entered and eight left, including several steal/egg titles such as Swim For Eggs and Drive an Egg.
Games 43-84 days old have a low median position percentile (22), well behind the 0-14-day group (60).
patterns: Selling currency packs and updating frequently tend to go with higher positions among games of the same age.
Luck passes and passes priced above about 349 R$ may go with lower positions, suggesting expensive launch monetization costs reach.
Co-op loops tend to rank higher, and horror and hatch/collect loops have strong medians, while steal and simulation-job loops have weak ones today.
No association reaches significance after correction on this chart, so all Up-and-Coming ideas stay in the 'may' to 'tends to' range.

outliers.name: HUNTRESS 🕷️ [NIGHTMARE]
outliers.note: Jumped 44 places at 108 days old, well past the usual breakout window; a horror update or creator push likely revived it.

outliers.name: [⛩️W3]  +1 Karate Evolution
outliers.note: A top-five '+1' incremental with 28 passes, against both the '+1' and the luck/expensive-pass patterns; its weekly world updates may carry it.

summary: Breakout charts favor the newest games while Top Earning efficiency rises with age, so games may pull players first and monetize later.

The steal/egg template keeps showing reach without revenue: weak Top Earning efficiency, falling young clones on Top Trending and Up-and-Coming, and only the original Steal An Egg holding the top of Most Popular.
Higher product and pass prices go with longer Most Popular stays and better Top Earning efficiency, while expensive passes may hurt Up-and-Coming reach, so pricing may need to rise as a game matures.
Complexity goes with both Most Popular staying power and Top Earning efficiency, the clearest sign that depth pays off over time.
progressions: Top Trending to Most Popular is the largest flow (52 entries, median 2 days later).
Up-and-Coming to Top Trending follows closely (49 entries, median 2 days).
Up-and-Coming to Most Popular (30, median 4 days) and Top Earning to Top Trending (34, median 5 days) come next; Most Popular rarely feeds the other charts (10 each).
